stories.headline: Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to Washington as the US-China trade truce is extended

sources.body:
US President Donald Trump has greeted his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping with a military flyover and 100ft (30m) red carpet to kick off their three-day summit in Washington.

In a rare move, Trump welcomed Xi's entourage at the airport as the US Air Force band marched on the tarmac and US and Chinese flags flew.

Trump and First Lady Melania Trump welcomed Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday evening in Maryland.

The high-stakes visit - Xi's first trip to Washington since 2015 - is expected to include closed-door meetings, a state dinner, and plenty to discuss, from AI, to the Iran war and Taiwan, and an extended trade truce.

The leader of Chinese Communist Party touched down in an Air China plane at 17:39 local time (22:39 BST). The colour and honour guard marched up to the aircraft and stood on both sides of the red carpet as two limos pulled up.

Xi and Peng exited their plane and the two couples shook hands. They spoke briefly before walking side by side down the red carpet and posing for photos.

Two B-1s flew over as the Army Air Force Band played the US national anthem. The supersonic aircraft are a key part of the US's combat arsenal.

After exchanging pleasantries, the two couples departed in separate vehicles to Washington.

This is the first time since 1962 that a US president has personally welcomed a foreign leader at the base, signalling the importance that Trump is giving this visit.

In 1962, then-President John F Kennedy greeted British PM Harold Macmillan.

Also on Wednesday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the US and China will extend their trade truce to January. The agreement, which saw Trump lower tariff rates on some goods in exchange for Xi loosening restrictions on rare earth minerals, was set to expire 10 November.

Bessent, who spoke after meeting Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng, said the two discussed if there can eventually be a more substantive trade deal between the two countries.

In a written statement published by China's state news agency Xinhua, Xi said both China and the US are "great nations, and their people are great people".

"The two countries should be partners rather than rivals," he said.

Melania Trump has said she has been involved intimately with the planning of the itinerary. She told Fox News that Trump made the decision to personally greet Xi himself at the airport "because they have a great relationship".

Xi is accompanied on the visit by Cai Qi, a member of the party's Politburo Standing Committee who's widely seen as his right-hand man, Vice Premier He Lifeng, Foreign Minister Wang Yi, as well as other delegates and ambassadors from Beijing.

"Realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can fully coexist, reinforce each other and benefit the world," Xi said in the statement carried by Xinhua, where he also expressed confident that the visit would "yield fruitful results".

It is unclear if Xi has brought any business executives with him. Bringing Chinese firms to the US may also raise questions about Chinese business practices, subsidies and overcapacity, all of which may draw more fire and questions than Xi or his party would like.
sources.headline: Trump offers warm welcome as China's Xi arrives for US visit

sources.body:
President lays out red carpet as treasury secretary announces extension of ‘Busan agreement’ pausing trade war hostilities

AI, trade, Taiwan and climate: what will and won’t be on agenda at Trump-Xi summit

Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US, taking the unusual step of greeting the Chinese leader on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews to kick off his state visit to Washington.

Xi’s plane was met with a lavish arrival ceremony that included a 30-metre-long (100ft) red carpet flanked by US service members, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers and a presentation of the flags and national anthems of both countries.

US presidents typically welcome foreign leaders at the White House, but Trump and the first lady, Melania, traveled to the the military base in Maryland, just outside Washington, to personally shake hands with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday evening.

Xi’s visit comes as world leaders gather in New York for the United Nations general assembly , although the Chinese leader will not address the meeting. He has attended the UNGA just once since becoming president in 2012.

“It’s pretty notable that Xi Jinping is ⁠coming to Washington in the same week as the general assembly, but does not feel bothered to come up to New York,” Richard Gowan of the International Crisis Group told Reuters. “I think a lot of people will say: ‘Where is the real center of decision-making?’”

Scott ⁠Bessent, the US treasury secretary, announced that the US ⁠and ​China agreed on Wednesday to extend the so-called Busan ⁠agreement – a temporary trade truce between the world’s two biggest economies.

Bessent, who met the Chinese ‌vice-premier He Lifeng earlier on Wednesday, told Fox News the agreement would be extended until 10 January, two months after it was due to expire.

The pageantry will continue with a formal state welcome on the South Lawn of the White House, private tea with the US president and first lady, and a tour of the National Archives, among other special events.

The simmering trade war is one of many thorny issues Trump and Xi must confront during the visit, including the race in artificial intelligence development and geopolitical instability during the two-day visit.

The White House has invited major tech leaders, such as executives from OpenAI, Apple, xAI, Microsoft, Nvidia, Meta and others, to a state dinner being held for Xi on Thursday.

There was one discordant note in the carefully orchestrated arrival ceremony, when Trump visibly winced at the sound of a US military jet flying overhead as he stood alongside Xi on the red carpet, listening to the US national anthem. Video of the moment showed that while Trump recoiled from the sound of the flyover, Xi remained impassive, as did the wives of both men.

The moment, which was widely mocked online, was captured on a White House livestream but not included in the edited highlights of the ceremony released by Trump’s aides later.

The US and China have long been competing to develop increasingly powerful technology, but the race to further AI has become a major topic among tech companies – especially after several executives came forward to warn about the dangers of rapid development.
sources.headline: Trump greets Xi Jinping on arrival in rare move as US-China trade truce extended

sources.body: US President Donald Trump personally welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping at a military airfield outside Washington on Wednesday, kicking off a lavish state visit focused on trade, artificial intelligence and Iran, as the two powers seek to preserve a fragile diplomatic and economic truce.
sources.headline: Trump gives Xi rare airport welcome as Chinese leader begins US state visit

stories.headline: Iran warns it could expand the war to the Indian Ocean while signaling openness to talks

sources.body: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei says the US has been given a five-day deadline to meet Tehran’s conditions for opening the Strait of Hormuz.
sources.headline: Iran threatens to expand war to ‘Indian Ocean and beyond’ if attacked again

sources.body: Iran may expand the Mideast war to the Indian Ocean if the US or Israel attacks again, an adviser to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned Thursday, hours before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addresses the UN General Assembly. President Donald Trump, in his speech, threatened to “annihilate” the Islamic Republic if a peace deal was not reached. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.
sources.headline: Live: Iran warns of expanding war to Indian Ocean if US and Israel attacks again

sources.body:
Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran is ready for dialogue and diplomacy ‘but without the language of force’

Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, turned the tables on Donald Trump, describing the US as the true bully and terrorist in the Middle East while insisting that Iran had always shown a commitment to the negotiating table.

In a defiant speech to the UN general assembly in New York, his first since the US and Israel launched an all-out war on Iran, Pezeshkian repeatedly vowed that Tehran would never bend the knee to the US.

But he balanced defiance with a willingness to talk, saying: “It must be understood by President Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations but without the language of force.”

On Tuesday, the US president had told the UN he was weighing whether to “annihilate” Iran, but went on to hail renewed talks between Tehran and Washington’s negotiators.

A surprise three-hour meeting between Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and the US special envoy Steve Witkoff on the sidelines of the assembly the same day was regarded as constructive by both sides. It was the first such meeting since June, but did not stop the US delegation from walking out at the start of Pezeshkian’s speech.

The Iranian president did not go into any details about the talks, but conveyed the impression that he was focused on winning the support of Iran’s Arab neighbours for the proposals Tehran has drawn up for the future of the strait of Hormuz , the vital waterway that has been intermittently blockaded since the start of the war, causing global energy prices to soar.

He made it clear Iran could not tolerate the strait being used to transport arms that could then be used against it, a statement that suggests the Islamic republic will demand the right to inspect ships travelling through the strait in the future. Iran’s goal, he said, was to live independently.

Pezeshkian accused Washington of “terrorism” for assassinating the supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the start of the war. He held up photographs of the dead leader and more than 150 schoolchildren killed in the opening days of the conflict, before insisting Tehran had never started a war.

“We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists,” he said. “Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed upon our country.”

He said Iran had the right to pursue a peaceful civil nuclear programme and it did not want to build nuclear weapons.

He repeatedly argued that the answer to regional security lay in agreement within the region and not with outsiders such as the US. Iran did not see its neighbours as security rivals, he said, but as partners in security. “In today’s world, those that are unable to defend themselves will be trampled upon,” he added.

Iran has repeatedly targeted US allies in the region since the start of the war.

Insisting Iran was the true victim of terrorism, Pezeshkian questioned why “Israel kills, yet Iran is subject to sanction”. He added: “They kill, we are sanctioned. Iran did not seek special treatment but wanted equal rights.”
sources.headline: Iran’s president hits out at ‘bully’ Trump in UN speech but signals willingness to talk

stories.headline: Australia investigates alleged breach of a government health portal by an OpenAI agent

sources.body:
AI doesn’t think. It just predicts the next word in a sequence based on pattern recognition. We use the word "thinking" because it’s easier to explain.

When the tech is given autonomy to carry out tasks, mistakes can happen because it has no true understanding of what it is being asked - the trouble is we don’t really know what it’s thinking either.

When an AI thinks, it’s going through a chain of planning actions. It provides logs to tell us mere humans what it’s doing, but here’s the rub: we can’t say for sure that those logs are accurate.

We all know AI hallucinates, so what if it’s doing one thing and saying another? What if it just summarises incorrectly?

And critically, these frontier models are doing heaps of things so quickly, we’re relying on the AI to decide what to tell us anyway.

All of this has some people quite worried about the direction things are headed.
sources.headline: Australia launches urgent review after OpenAI program hacks government health portal

sources.body:
Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has revealed a security breach of a government website containing Australians’ health data by an “AI agent”, less than a day after signing a joint appeal for “urgent global guardrails” around artificial intelligence.

Albanese co-signed the “ A Call for Control of Frontier AI Models ” statement on Tuesday together with 21 signatories including Canada, Spain and Germany, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) meeting in New York.

Addressing reporters on Wednesday, Albanese said the agent, developed by OpenAI, accessed public and non-public data on the government’s Medicare portal in June.

Australia’s Labor government is tightening tech regulations with new online safety laws, age bans and proposed digital duty of care frameworks.

Albanese said he had spoken to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express Canberra’s “extreme concern” about the hack and disappointment that the company took three months to admit the breach.

OpenAI responded in the hours after the news conference, stating that while it was still investigating, there was no evidence patient records were accessed.

The company’s review had identified activity involving several Australian government websites and services as its “models attempted to look up answers”, it said.

The leaders of artificial intelligence companies warned of the risks of unregulated AI development before a 15-member UN Security Council meeting on Wednesday.

One of them, Yoshua Bengio, a Canadian considered one of the ‘Godfathers of AI’ and co-chair of the Independent International Scientific Panel, spoke of the “unprecedented threat” and the “real and imminent” dangers of the technology.

China’s UN ambassador Fu Cong told the meeting that Beijing believed continuous improvement of regulatory frameworks, emergency response and cross-border cooperation on AI was needed.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the United Kingdom was ready to lead an international effort to establish AI standards.

“We’ve all heard the warnings which we must heed… so we have to rise to this moment,” he said, but added he also wanted the UK to pursue the benefits of AI.

French President Emmanuel Macron warned against allowing the United States and China to dominate decision-making around AI during his speech to the assembly on Wednesday.

US President Donald Trump is at odds with many of his counterparts, comparing the dangers of AI to climate change , which he has called a hoax.

He also proposed rebranding the term AI to SI, or “super intelligence”, during his address to the UNGA on Tuesday, and earlier said he planned to appoint an AI adviser.

In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump said the US was leading the AI race over China , that he was “not going to stifle Growth”, but added ⁠that the US would be careful.

White House science and technology adviser Michael Kratsios echoed Trump in remarks to the UN Security Council on Wednesday.

“You cannot govern technology you do not understand. This body and others like it should focus on sharing best practices to build domestic capacity, not establishing a global regulatory scheme,” he said.
sources.headline: Australia says OpenAI agent hacked Medicare portal

sources.body: An AI agent developed by OpenAI gained unauthorised access to an Australian government website in June, accessing public and non-public files in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as the first known case of an AI agent hacking a government system.
sources.headline: OpenAI AI agent breached Australian government website, PM says

stories.headline: Russia strikes Kyiv and Kharkiv as Ukraine braces for another difficult winter

sources.body: Russia on Thursday hit Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones, killing two people, while a strike on a farm in the Kharkiv region killed six, according to Ukrainian officials. As autumn approaches, Ukrainians are bracing for a tough winter following Moscow's intensifying attacks on the country's energy infrastructure.
sources.headline: Russia slams Kyiv with ballistic missiles as Ukrainians brace for harsh winter

stories.headline: Pakistan launches air strikes in Afghanistan after alleged Taliban drone attacks

sources.body:
Pakistan said it carried out air strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan used to store and launch drones.

Pakistani air strikes on Afghanistan have killed at least four people, a spokesman for the Afghan Taliban government said, promising to deliver an “appropriate response”.

Pakistan said on Thursday it carried out air strikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan used to store and launch drones, some of which were used in cross-border attacks.

Afghanistan’s Taliban government spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid said the air strikes targeted Kandahar, Paktia and Khost provinces.

A resident in Kandahar city told the AFP news agency that an air strike hit the city in southern Afghanistan. The resident said they heard a jet, then a large explosion, followed by a fire in the centre of Kandahar city, AFP reported.

Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said air strikes were “deliberate, precise, calibrated, and proportionate, and strictly limited to identified military objectives directly linked to the attempted attacks against Pakistan”.

He condemned a “deliberate and unlawful incursion into Pakistan by drones” on Wednesday.

“This constitutes a blatant violation of Pakistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and is a grave and unacceptable act of aggression,” he said.

Taliban officials denied that their government launched drones against Pakistan on Wednesday.

The air raids on Thursday were carried out as tensions grow between the former allies over attacks by armed groups in Pakistan, which triggered their worst fighting in years in February.

Islamabad accuses Kabul of harbouring fighters who stage cross-border attacks, but Afghanistan’s Taliban government denies harbouring anti-Pakistani armed groups and says the attacks are Pakistan’s internal problem.

An attack on a police facility in northwestern Pakistan last week that killed at least 21 people has reignited ⁠fighting between the countries after nearly three months of ⁠relative calm. A Pakistan Taliban faction claimed responsibility for the blast and subsequent gun battle .

On Monday, air raids targeting three locations in northeastern Afghanistan killed three civilians in the Nurgal district of Kunar province, Afghan officials said. Islamabad said it killed 28 “terrorists”.

The escalation threatens mediation efforts by China, Turkiye, Qatar and Saudi Arabia to broker a lasting peace between the two neighbours.

Relations between the former allies have been strained since the fighting in February, the worst for years.
sources.headline: Afghanistan vows to respond after Pakistani air strikes kill four

sources.body: Pakistan launched air strikes Thursday on 10 sites in Afghanistan in what Islamabad said was a retaliation for a drone attack by Afghanistan's Taliban forces on a border post. A Taliban government spokesman denied the allegation and said Pakistan's latest strikes killed four civilians in Afghanistan's southern and eastern provinces.
sources.headline: Pakistan launches air strikes in Afghanistan, killing civilians, Taliban says

stories.headline: Federal judge temporarily blocks the White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico

sources.body:
A judge has ordered the Trump administration to immediately reinstate access to the White House for three news organisations barred from the building last week by the president.

A District of Columbia court issued a temporary restraining order against the ban, meaning CNN, MS NOW and Politico must have their access restored for 14 days, after ruling the move "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".

The three outlets launched a legal challenge after their reporters had their passes for the White House confiscated and were denied access.

The Trump administration defended the move in court, accusing the outlets of publishing false information and threatening national security - an argument the court rejected.

The White House is yet to comment on the ruling, and lawyers acting for the president may take further legal action.

Judge Timothy Kelly ruled CNN, Politico and MS NOW were "likely to succeed" in showing the White House had not exercised "adequate due process" in implementing the ban.

He also cast doubt on the Trump administration's arguments that the bans were motivated by national security concerns, pointing out the president made no mention of that in his initial announcement.

The ruling continued: "The record lacks factual support for Defendants' contention that the revocation of Plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security or that national security will be endangered if the Court orders their passes reinstated while this litigation proceeds."

In its defence of the ban, the Trump administration cited a number of articles published by the outlets, including some about construction at the White House, including work on a new ballroom.

The judge said that "in most cases" the stories the White House took issue with were written by journalists who "did not even hold card passes" - and in the remaining cases, the Trump administration did not demonstrate "reason to believe that the reporter's possession of the hard pass was integral to the stories identified".

In its original filing, the Trump administration cited declarations from defence department officials supporting the ban - but the judge said they had "no direct knowledge of how reporters operate in the White House, or about any of the facts at issue here".

Ted Boutrous, the lawyer representing the news outlets, told CNN : "This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law."

On Monday, major US TV networks pulled out of White House pool duties in protest at the ban. The arrangement sees media organisations share material with each other to save on costs and space when broadcasting presidential events to the American public.

Forty-nine media organisations - including CBS News, The New York Times and Fox News - also filed a legal brief in support of CNN, MS NOW and Politico's lawsuit.

Trump frequently criticises news organisations, and his administration has launched legal action against a series of outlets, including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal and the BBC.
sources.headline: Judge temporarily overturns Trump's White House media ban

sources.body:
Trump-nominated judge rules that outlets are likely to succeed in claim they were denied due process.

A United States judge has blocked President Donald Trump’s ban on three news outlets from the White House, ordering his administration to immediately restore their access pending a later court hearing.

Issuing a temporary restraining order early on Thursday, US District Judge Timothy J Kelly said CNN, MS NOW and Politico were likely to prevail in their legal challenge to Trump’s ban on several grounds, including that it violated their due process rights.

Kelly said the outlets had made a convincing case that they were stripped of their credentials without due process and were likely to suffer “irreparable harm” in the absence of the temporary order.

Kelly, who was nominated by Trump during his first term in 2017, also found there was a public interest in blocking the ban “given the importance of the free press”.

Rejecting the Trump administration’s claim that the outlets had been barred to protect national security, Kelly said the government’s argument lacked “factual support”.

“Defendants offer no declarations or other support – classified or unclassified – explaining how any of the reporting they identified in their letters to Plaintiffs damaged the national security,” Kelly said in the ruling.

Kelly ruled that the Trump administration should “immediately return, reinstate, and restore” the outlets’ access to the White House.

Kelly imposed the injunction for 14 days, pending further proceedings.

Theodore Boutrous, the lawyer representing the outlets, welcomed the ruling as a vindication of the “freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law”.

“We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action,” Boutrous said in a statement.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump, who has launched a slew of attacks on the media as president, on Friday announced that he had barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from covering the White House, citing their reporting of unspecified “fake news”.

Trump later claimed in a news conference that the outlets produced “negative news” and sought to “diminish” his administration and the Republican Party.

CNN, Politico and MS NOW on Monday announced they had jointly filed a lawsuit seeking to overturn the ban, arguing it violated their free speech and due process rights.
sources.headline: US judge blocks Trump’s White House ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico

stories.headline: FDA advisers back Galleri cancer blood test but remain divided over its effectiveness

sources.body: A Food and Drug Administration committee backed a cancer blood test called Galleri but was split on how well it works. The test is awaiting a final decision by the FDA.
sources.headline: One blood test could screen you for 50 cancers. Here’s why it’s controversial.

stories.headline: Republicans reportedly shift Senate campaign priorities away from Georgia and North Carolina

sources.body: The National Republican Senatorial Committee is shifting its focus away from the North Carolina and Georgia Senate races as it works to shore up red states like Texas and flip other Democratic-held seats. In a closed-door meeting Wednesday, Sen. Tim Scott, the chair of the NRSC, told Senate Republicans that the campaign arm will focus its spending going forward on defending GOP seats in Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa and Texas and trying to flip the Democratic-held seats of Michigan and New Hampshire, according to four people in the room who were granted anonymity to share private details. That list notably leaves out North Carolina GOP nominee Michael Whatley’s battle against Democrat Roy Cooper and Georgia GOP nominee Mike Collins’ effort to unseat Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff . Scott’s briefing is the clearest sign yet that Republicans have deprioritized the two states, as POLITICO has reported , while senior Republicans grow increasingly resigned to the possibility of losing those races. It’s a remarkable shift: President Donald Trump carried Georgia twice in 2016 and 2024 and North Carolina over the last three presidential elections. In deprioritizing North Carolina, the NRSC is effectively ceding a state that Democrats haven’t won in the Senate since 2008. Still, other GOP groups with massive war chests, including Trump’s MAGA Inc., could pick up the slack. Scott also shared with the senators polling showing Republicans are locked in tight battles in several other key races, which tracks with much of the public polling, according to the four people. For example, one poll found that GOP Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio is still trailing former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown. Scott also showed polling indicating Republican John Sununu is essentially neck-and-neck with Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, a seat Republicans are laser-focused on trying to flip. The NRSC didn't initially respond to a request for comment. In a statement provided after publication, NRSC Communications Director Joanna Rodriguez said: “This completely fabricated story should be retracted and Politico should be embarrassed. Chairman Scott didn’t make any spending announcements at lunch and he praised Michael Whatley as an example of a candidate who has polling momentum on his side.” “As Roy Cooper said earlier this year about U.S. Senate races in North Carolina, 'Democrats are often ahead until they are not.' And then just last week Cooper, correctly, observed, 'We know a lot of undecided voters lean Republican.' We’re confident we will have the resources to get our message out to North Carolina voters and win,” said Whatley Spokesman DJ Griffin in a statement. Collins' campaign did not respond to a request for comment. Georgia GOP party chair Josh McKoon dismissed the notion that his state was being deprioritized by Republicans in Washington, even as he acknowledged beating Ossoff will be a challenge. “Every cycle, someone in Washington leaks that they’re thinking about moving money,” he said in a text message. “What matters is who shows up — and what the actual numbers say.” Senate Majority Leader John Thune is set to headline a fundraiser for Collins in Atlanta on Thursday, alongside the state’s popular Republican governor, Brian Kemp. The Collins campaign is also making the case that one in 10 Georgia voters — who backed Trump in 2024 and plan to vote for Jackson — are still "up for grabs,” according to a memo obtained by POLITICO . “The goal in Georgia is to strike a balance where you are spending as little for Senate as possible while not derailing Rick Jackson’s, so far, very strong bid for Governor in a difficult environment,” said a GOP pollster granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape. Public polling shows the governor’s race has much tighter margins, with Jackson leading Democratic nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms in some recent surveys . Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas), who lost his Senate primary to Trump-backed Ken Paxton, was also in the room. He later told POLITICO that the party has to make tough decisions. “At some point I think the people spending that money are going to have to make hard choices and figure out where the money can have the biggest impact, and certainly Texas is the most expensive,” Cornyn said.
sources.headline: NRSC Chair Tim Scott leaves Georgia, North Carolina off his list of top Senate targets

stories.headline: Spanish former prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero says seized jewelry was a 2007 gift from Saudi Arabia's king

El expresidente del Gobierno, en un escrito dirigido al juez, que le mantiene investigado en el <i>caso Plus Ultra</i>, y que ha avanzado EL PAÍS, sostiene que una docena de piezas valiosas halladas durante el registro en su despacho el pasado mes de mayo son <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-23/estas-son-las-12-joyas-que-zapatero-senala-como-un-regalo-del-rey-saudi-en-2007.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-23/estas-son-las-12-joyas-que-zapatero-senala-como-un-regalo-del-rey-saudi-en-2007.html">un regalo del monarca saudí Abdulá Bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud (fallecido en 2015)</a>. Pide a la Audiencia Nacional que solicite la cooperación del país para acreditar su relato.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-23/zapatero-asegura-al-juez-que-las-joyas-son-un-regalo-de-arabia-saudi-de-2007.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><h3>Calama envía a prisión provisional al financiero neerlandés clave en el ‘caso Plus Ultra’</h3><p>En el marco de esta investigación, el juez ha acordado enviar a prisión provisional al banquero neerlandés Simon Leendert Verhoeven, detenido el martes por las autoridades alemanas, "una vez se materialice su entrega". "Se trata", prosigue el escrito de Zapatero, "de una diligencia de comprobaci�n perfectamente delimitada que, de considerarse necesaria, permitir�a despejar definitivamente la �nica cuesti�n f�ctica que dio origen a esta pieza separada: la procedencia de las joyas".

Con respecto al resto de piezas intervenidas, el ex l�der del PSOE explica que tienen poco valor y "proceden de antepasados y recuerdos de familia y forman parte del ajuar familiar, al igual que alg�n que otro obsequio que ha recibido por diferentes relaciones de amistad". "En todo caso, todos estos efectos deben considerarse de todo punto irrelevantes", apostilla.

stories.headline: Spain's government and opposition trade blame over the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen in Madrid

sources.body: <p>El drama del desahucio de Maricarmen, de 87 años, ha generado una gran conmoción especialmente entre sectores progresistas, que apuntan al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez por no haber sido capaz de frenarlo. Preguntado por este asunto en Nueva York, en la habitual rueda de prensa durante la cumbre de la ONU en Nueva York, Sánchez ha responsabilizado directamente a la Comunidad de Madrid y el Ayuntamiento de Madrid, en manos del PP, contra los que ha cargado de forma dura porque cree que podían haber impedido el desahucio o buscar una solución alternativa y no han hecho nada. “El desahucio de Maricarmen es una tragedia social que no podemos aceptar como país”, ha arrancado el presidente, que llevaba preparado un largo discurso sobre este asunto que genera mucha tensión especialmente a sus potenciales votantes. “Hay que decir que hay dos administraciones competentes en la protección de personas vulnerables como Maricarmen, el Ayuntamiento de Madrid y la Comunidad de Madrid, que están mas preocupados en comprar aticazos de 200 metros de terraza pero han hecho caso omiso a una tragedia social que debería ser resuelta”.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-23/pedro-sanchez-comparece-antes-de-su-discurso-en-naciones-unidas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Sánchez carga contra Ayuso y Almeida por la “tragedia social” del desahucio de Maricarmen: “Están más preocupados en comprar aticazos”

sources.body:
Un día después de ser expulsada del piso en el que vivió durante 71 años , Maricarmen no tiene dónde dormir. Ha pasado su primera noche en el Hospital Gregorio Marañón de Madrid en un delicado estado de salud y no ha podido recoger sus pertenencias. Salió únicamente con una sábana y en camilla, una imagen desoladora que se ha convertido en la chispa de una gran movilización social y que ha encendido también la batalla política sobre la vivienda, primera preocupación para los españoles según las encuestas.

El hartazgo y la indignación se hicieron patentes tan solo unas horas después del desalojo de esta anciana de 87 años, cuando miles de personas salieron a las calles en 12 ciudades en una protesta prácticamente improvisada . En Madrid, la concentración convocada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas frente al polémico ático adquirido por la Comunidad de Madrid llegó a sacar a la calle a unas 10.000 personas, según la Delegación del Gobierno.

La abogada de Maricarmen, Beatriz Duro, ha reclamado precisamente que este caso "sirva de ejemplo y permita poner de relieve una realidad vergonzosa que estamos viviendo desde hace muchísimos años en nuestro país: se desahucia a las personas diariamente sin alternativa habitacional y no se regula ni se legisla para garantizar el derecho a la vivienda", ha apuntado en RNE.

Aunque el desahucio de Maricarmen ha sido especialmente mediático, no es, ni mucho menos, una realidad aislada. Cada día se ejecutan 80 expulsiones como esta en nuestro país, "80 maricarmen al día que tienen que abandonar su hogar", según ha denunciado el portavoz del Sindicato de Inquilinas, Fernando de los Santos, en TVE. Y solo contando aquellos con resolución judicial. No computan, por ejemplo, los casos de inquilinos que reciben un burofax y dejan sus casas silenciosamente.

En el primer trimestre de 2026 se dieron, según los datos del Consejo General del Poder Judicial, 4.005 desahucios. Los más numerosos, un 65%, por impago de alquiler, en medio de una subida de precios que parece no tocar techo. La ley de vivienda permite topar los precios, pero esto solo se ha aplicado en Cataluña y parcialmente en País Vasco, Navarra y Galicia. No en la Comunidad de Madrid, donde el precio por metro cuadrado es el más caro de España.

Las administraciones, entretanto, se culpan las unas a otras: el Ministerio de Vivienda a la Comunidad de Madrid y viceversa . De los Santos ha recordado que los desahucios no son "una inevitabilidad natural". "Hay unos responsables directos, no se pueden pasar la pelota" . En primer lugar, ha señalado al delegado del Gobierno en Madrid, Francisco Martín, que "debe dimitir" por un operativo policial "violento" y desmedido, con 12 furgones policiales y más de 100 efectivos.

Pero también ha mencionado a la presidenta madrileña, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, que "se está comprando un ático y tenía dinero de sobra" para comprar el piso de Maricarmen y que "se reúne con fondos buitre"; al alcalde, José Luis Martínez Almeida, por no ofrecer una solución habitacional alternativa, y al Gobierno central. Concretamente al PSOE , que se abstuvo cuando el Congreso debatió el pasado 15 de septiembre una proposición de Sumar para prohibir la compra especulativa por parte de fondos buitres .
sources.headline: El desahucio de Maricarmen conmociona a Espa�a y pone sobre la mesa el drama de la vivienda: "Se dan a diario"

sources.body:
Isabel Díaz Ayuso durante el acto de inicio del curso político del PP de Madrid 

Isabel Díaz Ayuso ha encontrado en la ley el parapeto con el que responder a Pedro Sánchez.  Horas después de que el presidente del Gobierno señalara a la presidenta madrileña y al alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida, como responsables políticos de la “tragedia social” que representa  el desahucio de Maricarmen, Ayuso ha devuelto la pelota a La Moncloa. El desalojo de la mujer de 87 años, ha sostenido, no es una decisión de su Gobierno, sino la ejecución de una orden judicial por parte de la Policía Nacional. Y si las reglas no gustan, ha venido a decir, Sánchez y sus socios han tenido ocho años para cambiarlas.

“Ayer se produjo un desahucio de los 25.500 que se ejecutan todos los años en España, a manos de la Policía Nacional, que la gestiona el Gobierno. Por orden judicial, no por otro motivo, no es una decisión nuestra”, ha argumentado la dirigente popular durante un acto del Círculo de Empresarios de Madrid. “En cumplimiento de una ley y de unas leyes que este Gobierno y sus socios han tenido ocho años para modificar, si no estaban de acuerdo con ellas”, ha añadido.

La respuesta de Ayuso busca cerrar por la vía de las competencias una cuestión que Sánchez había planteado en términos políticos. El presidente no discutió quién ejecutó el lanzamiento. Su reproche fue otro. Que las administraciones gobernadas por el PP en Madrid, tanto la Comunidad como el Ayuntamiento, podían haber hecho más para evitar que una mujer de 87 años acabara en la calle.

Ahí es donde el caso de Maricarmen toca una fibra más incómoda para el PP madrileño. Porque el desahucio puede ser, jurídicamente, el cumplimiento de una resolución judicial. Pero la política de vivienda que ha llevado hasta ese escenario forma parte de un debate mucho más amplio, y en ese debate Ayuso y Almeida llevan años dejando clara su posición.

En octubre de 2021, Almeida lo resumió en una sola palabra. Fue como respuesta a Más Madrid, quien previamente le había reprochado al alcalde en las redes sociales que “no va a hacer nada para regular los precios de los alquileres en la ciudad”. A lo que el regidor respondió: “Exacto”.

No era un desliz. El alcalde ha defendido desde entonces que intervenir los precios provoca inseguridad jurídica y termina expulsando viviendas del mercado. Ayuso ha mantenido un discurso prácticamente paralelo desde la Comunidad de Madrid. Ha presentado los límites al alquiler como un “ataque directo contra la propiedad privada”, ha rechazado declarar zonas tensionadas y ha convertido la negativa a intervenir los precios en uno de los rasgos distintivos de su política de vivienda.

Ese es el contexto en el que ahora Ayuso reivindica el “Estado de Derecho”, la “seguridad jurídica”, “la ley y el orden” para responder a Sánchez. No porque exista una contradicción entre cumplir una orden judicial y defender una determinada política de vivienda, sino porque el episodio vuelve a colocar frente a frente dos concepciones políticas sobre qué pueden -y qué deben- hacer las administraciones ante el problema de la vivienda.
sources.headline: Ayuso se escuda en la ley y devuelve a Sánchez la responsabilidad por el desahucio de Maricarmen

sources.headline: Activan dos cazas espa�oles en Ruman�a por la presencia de drones rusos en territorio OTAN

sources.body:
Uno de los cazas españoles F-18 del Ejército del Aire y del Espacio desplegados en Rumanía

Una patrulla de cazas F-18 del Ejército del Aire y del Espacio desplegados en Rumania ha sido activada esta madrugada ante una amenaza real de drones detectados en la frontera con Ucrania.

Según ha informado el Ministerio de Defensa de Rumanía, el sistema de vigilancia radar se percató de un grupo de objetivos aéreos que operaban al norte de la localidad de Chilia Veche, en territorio de Ucrania. El Centro Nacional Militar de Mando lanzó una alerta a la población del norte del distrito de Tulcea a las 04.41 horas. La alerta cesó a las 05:44h.

Aunque en un primer comunicado el Ministerio de Defensa de Ucrania anunció que el dron no había invadido el cielo ucraniano, una actualización ha especificado que el aparato se desplazó dentro del espacio aéreo nacional durante aproximadamente cuatro minutos, tras lo cual se estrelló cerca de la localidad de Solca, en el condado de Suceava, sin causar víctimas ni daños materiales.

Los equipos de intervención del Ministerio del Interior llegaron al lugar, aseguraron el perímetro e identificaron el dron de pequeño tamaño, sin que se registrara fuego en el lugar del impacto.

La alerta activó a dos de los siete cazas españoles desplegados en la base aérea Mihail Kogălniceanu, muy próxima al mar Negro. Las aeronaves forman parte del Destacamento Aéreo Táctico (DAT) Paznic, liderado por el teniente coronel Alberto Borja Calvo López, que fue desplegado el pasado mes de julio para contribuir en la misión de Policía Aérea Reforzada (eAP-72) de la OTAN, en el país balcánico.

El contingente lo forman cerca de 200 militares del Ejército del Aire y del Espacio, en función de las distintas fases del despliegue. El núcleo de la contribución aérea está formado por siete aviones F-18M del Ala 12, que permanecen en zona durante todo el despliegue. Además, durante los dos primeros meses de misión, el contingente está contando con el apoyo de un avión A400M del Ala 31.

La semana que viene, para el último tramo de la operación, se incorporarán tres helicópteros NH-90 del Ala 48, que asumirán cometidos de lucha contra sistemas aéreos no tripulados (C-UAS).

stories.headline: Morocco's monarchy-aligned PAM leads provisional election results amid low turnout

sources.body:
Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) took 97 out of 395 seats in parliament, as turnout falls to 38 percent.

Morocco’s monarchy-aligned Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) has won the most seats in parliamentary elections, according to provisional results.

PAM took 97 out of 395 seats in parliament, overtaking its senior coalition partner, the liberal National Rally of Independents (RNI), Interior Minister Abdelouafi Laftit announced on Thursday.

The RNI secured 66 seats and the Istiqlal Party took 65, according to the provisional results. The Justice and Development Party (PJD), a centrist Islamist party that won 13 seats in 2021, surged to 54.

Turnout fell to 38.02 percent from 50 percent in 2021, according to official data.

Under the 2011 constitution, King Mohammed VI appoints the prime minister from the largest party, putting PAM in line to lead the next government.

The vote was the first since deadly Gen Z-led protests last year, and the next government will face pressure to address everyday concerns, including jobs, wages and the cost of living.

It will also oversee billions of dollars in investment as Morocco prepares to cohost the 2030 World Cup.

Since no single party is expected to capture an absolute majority, the winner will need to build a coalition government. Portfolios are split among the political allies, but the palace traditionally keeps key posts such as defence and foreign affairs under royal control.

PAM leaders have ruled out another partnership with the RNI. The two parties have traded accusations over failed policies.

PAM campaigned on a $37bn platform promising 1 million new jobs, better wages and continued investment in healthcare and social protection.

One possible candidate for prime minister is PAM’s Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, who would become the Arab region’s second female head of government, after Tunisia’s Najla Bouden, if appointed.

Another potential candidate is Fouzi Lekjaa, the budget minister and head of the football federation, who joined PAM weeks before the vote.
sources.headline: Monarchy-aligned PAM leads in Morocco election provisional results

sources.body:
Una mujer deposita su voto durante las elecciones en Marruecos, en un colegio electoral de Rabat. / JALAL MORCHIDI / EFE

El Partido Autenticidad y Modernidad (PAM) ha ganado las elecciones legislativas marroquíes con 97 diputados , según los resultados provisionales anunciados la madrugada del jueves por el Ministerio del Interior. Esta formación, que quedó segunda en los comicios de 2021, ha logrado dar el sorpaso a la Agrupación Nacional de Independientes (RNI), que ha caído a segunda posición tras perder un tercio de diputados y quedarse con 66.

La abstención ha sido una de las grandes protagonistas de la jornada electoral: solo el 38% de los inscritos para poder votar ha participado en las elecciones . La cifra más baja en 20 años. La abstencion ha subido, especialmente por el desinterés o la desconfianza de una parte de la sociedad con los partidos políticos. Un divorcio evidente especialmente entre los más jóvenes : los que tienen entre 18 y 24 años solo han supuesto el 4% de todos los inscritos para poder participar en los comicios.

En Marruecos , el monarca es el encargado de elegir al presidente del Gobierno dentro del partido más votado . Algunos de los nombres que han figurado en las quinielas como posibles candidatos a la presidencia son el de Fouzi Lekjaa, ministro y presidente de la Federación de Fútbol marroquí , que ha sido uno de los protagonistas de la campaña electoral tras sumarse al PAM unas semanas antes de los comicios. Otro nombre es el de Fátima Ezzahra El Mansouri , también ministra y alcaldesa de Marrakech .

El PAM también se verá obligado a buscar en el Parlamento una coalición para llegar a la mayoría absoluta. El partido Istiqlal mantiene la tercera posición con 65 diputados . Los islamistas del PJD recuperan terreno político y logran quedar cuartos con 54 diputados, lo que supone 41 más que en las pasadas elecciones, cuando obtuvieron una de sus peores derrotas.
sources.headline: Cambio al frente del Gobierno de Marruecos tras unas elecciones con una abstención del 62%

stories.headline: Barcelona approves a phased increase in its cruise-passenger tax through 2030

sources.body:
L'Ajuntament de Barcelona ha aprovat apujar de forma progressiva la taxa turística als creuers que fan escala a la ciutat perquè el 2030 es paguin 24 euros per persona i dia .

Aquesta taxa, sumada als 6 euros de l'impost que recapta el govern, situa la quota total en 30 euros , el triple del que paguen ara.

La mesura vol desincentivar aquest tipus de creuers que passen poques hores a la ciutat i deixen pocs diners, pels problemes de massificació que generen als barris amb més pressió turística.

"Volem posar fi a un model de creuers d'escala que massifica l'espai públic i genera molèsties als veïns", ha justificat el tinent d'alcaldia d'Economia, Jordi Valls , en un debat a una comissió municipal.

El govern municipal del PSC ha comptat amb el suport de Junts i Esquerra , mentre que Barcelona en Comú, amb qui es va pactar la mesura abans de l'estiu , hi ha votat en contra perquè s'aplicarà de forma progressiva i no de cop . PP i Vox també hi han votat en contra.

Dels 30 euros de taxa que pagarà cada creuerista d'escala a Barcelona, 24 euros corresponen al recàrrec municipal -que és el que s'incrementarà de forma progressiva fins al 2030, mentre que els altres 6 són la part de l'impost que recapta la Generalitat.

Per poder tirar endavant aquest augment, el Parlament va aprovar al juliol una modificació de la llei que regula la taxa turística per tal que l'Ajuntament de Barcelona pugui ampliar el topall del recàrrec municipal.

La pujada de la taxa turística als creuers d'escala farà augmentar la recaptació municipal en 23,7 milions d'euros el 2031, segons càlculs de l'Ajuntament.

El tinent d'alcaldia Valls ha justificat l'augment progressiu de la taxa seguint les recomanacions del consell tributari i els informes dels serveis jurídics de l'Ajuntament per donar "predictibilitat i seguretat jurídica" a la mesura.

A més, ha recordat que des que l'Ajuntament va aprovar un recàrrec municipal a la taxa turística, tots els increments plantejats fins ara s'han fet també de forma progressiva.

Des dels Comuns, però, el regidor Marc Serra ha acusat el govern de l'alcalde Jaume Collboni de falta de valentia per no aplicar l'increment de cop l'any vinent: "Si haguessin estat valents, l'any que ve no tindríem creueristes d'escala massificant la ciutat".

El socialista Valls s'hi ha tornat assegurant que " mai ningú abans havia fet tant com aquest govern en fiscalitat turística", i ha afirmat que les quotes aprovades Barcelona recaptarà dels creuers més diners que Amsterdam o l'illa grega de Santorini.

A canvi del vot a favor de Junts, el govern municipal es compromet a incrementar el pressupost del pla d'ombres a la ciutat, i amb ERC s'ha negociat destinar més recursos al programa de reforç escolar .

En el debat a la comissió, el tinent d'alcaldia Jordi Valls ha anunciat que en compliment de l'acord amb el Port de Barcelona per reduir les terminals de creuers , a finals d'octubre deixarà de funcionar la terminal C, i a finals d'any la que opera al World Trade Center.

En la mateixa comissió, s'ha debatut la proposta d'ordenances fiscals per al 2027 que proposa el govern socialista de Barcelona i que preveu un increment del 30% de l'IBI als hotels amb valor cadastral més alt , passant de l'1,17% actual fins a l'1,3%.
sources.headline: 24 euros per creuerista d'escala: Barcelona aprova apujar la taxa progressivament fins al 2030

stories.headline: Sagrada Família acknowledges its planned grand staircase will affect more than one building

sources.body:
La construcció de l'escalinata de la Sagrada Família que ha de culminar la façana de la Glòria " afectarà més d'un edifici" . La Junta Constructora havia dit aquest dimarts en roda de premsa que en tenia prou amb l'enderroc i trasllat d'un sol bloc d'habitatges, però hores després ha rectificat .

Fonts del temple han matisat que l'enderroc de l'edifici del carrer Mallorca, propietat de Núñez i Navarro, que queda just davant del temple, és "clau i imprescindible" per fer l'escalinata, però apunten que "el projecte també comportarà afectacions en altres edificis de l'entorn".

La rectificació arriba després de la sorpresa que s'ha generat aquest dimarts quan, per primer cop, la Junta Constructora ha concretat l'abast dels seus plans . Fins ara, per culminar el temple tenien sota amenaça d'enderroc diversos edificis de les illes del davant, qualificats de zona verda segons el pla general metropolità del 1976.

"Fer l'escala ara és impossible perquè hi ha un edifici al davant", ha dit el director general de la Junta, Xavier Martínez , en la roda de premsa en què ha detallat que només amb el trasllat d'aquest edifici , propietat de Núñez i Navarro, n'hi hauria prou per fer l'escalinata.

En els últims mesos, la Sagrada Família, l'Ajuntament de Barcelona i els veïns afectats han estat negociant una solució , però segons Martínez, ara és el consistori qui ha de "moure peça".

Des de la Junta Constructora han plantejat l'enderroc i trasllat dels veïns d'aquest bloc a l'illa del costat , entre els carrers de Marina i Lepant, a un espai que és propietat del temple. En la roda de premsa no s'ha concretat qui pagarà l'operació.

Fonts municipals insisteixen en el diàleg a tres bandes per trobar "el millor encaix" del monument amb el barri, tenint en compte el pla urbanístic vigent i un entorn "amb molta pressió turística".

El consistori recorda que l'objectiu del govern municipal serà sempre "garantir el dret a l'habitatge" i que és des d'aquesta premissa que s'estan estudiant possibles alternatives. L'executiu de Jaume Collboni es va fixar l'objectiu d'arribar a un acord aquest mandat .

Amb la llicència d'obres que la Sagrada Família va acordar amb l'Ajuntament de Barcelona, la Junta Constructora no pot afrontar ni l'escalinata ni la decoració frontal de la façana de la Glòria. Per això també és important tancar un acord.

Els permisos vigents només permeten alçar les quatre torres que tindrà aquesta façana, que arribaran als 120 metres d'altura. Les torres estaran suportades al damunt de vuit columnes, que es volen començar a aixecar l'any vinent.

Per agilitzar les torres, la Sagrada Família ha dissenyat un prototip per assajar el mètode constructiu , ja que es preveu que s'alcin a partir de panells de pedra que aniran encaixant, igual que es va fer amb la torre de Jesús.

Per tot plegat, la Junta Constructora manté "el desig" que 10 anys sigui "un període més que suficient" per acabar la Sagrada Família, tot i que no es volen aventurar a donar una data exacta.

Més enllà de l'escalinata i les quatre torres, la façana de la Glòria comptarà amb una decoració escultòrica suspesa a l'aire que està pendent de definir.
sources.headline: La Sagrada Família rectifica i diu que culminar l'escalinata "afectarà més d'un edifici"

stories.headline: Poll finds Barcelonans dissatisfied with City Hall management, while Collboni remains the preferred mayoral candidate

sources.body:
Usuarios en el metro de Barcelona. / MANU MITRU / EPC

Los barceloneses suspenden la gestión del Ayuntamiento de su ciudad, según la encuesta del Gabinet d'Estudis Socials i Opinió Pública (GESOP) para EL PERIÓDICO . El consistorio que dirige el alcalde Jaume Collboni obtiene una nota de 4,8 y se queda por debajo de las valoraciones de los dos últimos años: un 5,3 en 2024 y un 5,2 en 2025.

El sondeo, elaborado entre el 10 y el 21 de septiembre a partir de 802 entrevistas, muestra que la valoración empeora en todas las franjas de edad . Los mayores de 60 años son los más satisfechos y los únicos que aprueban la gestión municipal con un 5,2, mientras que la nota más baja corresponde a los barceloneses de entre 30 y 44 años, con un 4,2. Los jóvenes de 18 a 29 años le dan un 4,4.

Solo los electores del PSC, los Comuns y ERC aprueban la gestión de Collboni. Los socialistas la puntúan con un 6,1, la misma nota que hace un año; los votantes de los Comuns, con un 5,5, y los de ERC, con un 5,1. Los que peor valoran la actuación municipal son los simpatizantes de Vox (con un 2,9) y los de Junts (con un 3,5).

La percepción sobre la evolución de Barcelona tampoco es alentadora . Un 61,9% de los barceloneses cree que la capital catalana ha empeorado en el último año, frente al 50,2% que opinaba lo mismo en 2024 y el 51,4% de 2025. Un 28,9% cree que la situación se mantiene y solo un 8,6% considera que ha mejorado.

Gente paseando por Arc de Triomf. / FERRAN NADEU / EPC

El deterioro se percibe especialmente entre los menores de 45 años. Un 67% de los barceloneses de entre 30 y 44 años cree que la ciudad está peor que hace un año y el porcentaje alcanza el 64,6% entre los jóvenes de 18 a 29 años. El pesimismo se modera con la edad: entre los mayores de 60 años baja hasta el 58,1%, mientras que un 13% de este grupo considera que Barcelona ha mejorado.

También existen diferencias claras según el recuerdo de voto. El pesimismo es especialmente elevado entre los electores de Vox, Junts y PP: el 91,2%, el 81,8% y el 70,9%, respectivamente, consideran que Barcelona está peor que hace un año. Entre los votantes de la CUP el porcentaje es del 66,6% y entre los de ERC, del 58,4%.

Entre los votantes de los Comuns la opinión está más repartida , ya que un 47,3% considera que la ciudad ha empeorado, un 40,2% que no ha sufrido cambios y un 12,5% que ha mejorado. También entre los socialistas la respuesta más frecuente es que Barcelona está peor: lo cree un 42,3%, frente al 37,9% que la ve igual y el 19,2% que considera que ha mejorado.

El pesimismo también se proyecta hacia el futuro . El 42,3% cree que Barcelona seguirá yendo a peor, mientras que el 38,5% sostiene que permanecerá igual que ahora. Solo un 12,9% se muestra optimista y cree que mejorará en 2027, cuando hay elecciones municipales.

Los jóvenes son los más desanimados: un 52,8% de los encuestados de entre 18 y 29 años augura un empeoramiento. Entre los mayores de 60 años, en cambio, cunde más la sensación de continuidad, ya que un 38,5% cree que la ciudad seguirá igual y un 33,9% que irá a peor.
sources.headline: Sondeo GESOP: Los barceloneses suspenden la gestión del Ayuntamiento y el 42% cree que Barcelona irá a peor

sources.body:
Los candidatos a la alcaldía de Barcelona en 2027: Jaume Collboni (PSC), Jordi Martí Galbis (Junts), Elisenda Alamany (ERC), Gerardo Pisarello (BComú), Jordi Aragonès (Aliança) y Daniel Sirera (PP) / EL PERIÓDICO

La popularidad de Jaume Collboni ha ido creciendo a medida que se hacía con el traje de alcalde. El líder del PSC es el candidato más citado por los barceloneses para revalidar su puesto tras las elecciones municipales, pero es también el dirigente municipal más conocido y el único al que los ciudadanos aprueban, según la encuesta del Gabinet d'Estudis Socials i Opinió Pública (GESOP) para EL PERIÓDICO .

El actual alcalde de la ciudad es el preferido para repetir en el cargo, ya que un 19,9% de los encuestados asegura que le gustaría que volviese a hacerse con la vara de mando tras pasar por las urnas. La candidata de ERC, Elisenda Alamany , y el cabeza de lista de los Comuns, Gerardo Pisarello , se disputan el segundo puesto con un 8,3% y un 8% de las preferencias, respectivamente.

El cuarto puesto lo ocupa un debutante: el cabeza de lista de la formación de extrema derecha Aliança Catalana, Jordi Aragonès , que reúne un 3,4% de las preferencias, por delante de la opción de Junts, Jordi Martí (2,7%), la del PP, Daniel Sirera (2,6%), y la de Vox, Gonzalo de Oro-Pulido (1%). Sin embargo, un 28% de los sondeados responde que no elegiría a ninguno de ellos, y un 22% no se pronuncia. El sondeo no recoge los datos de Laure Vega como candidata de la CUP porque fue proclamada el pasado 19 de septiembre, cuando la encuesta ya estaba en marcha.

La edad también marca diferencias. Collboni y Pisarello están prácticamente empatados entre los barceloneses de 30 a 44 años, con un 12,9% y un 12,4%, respectivamente, mientras que el líder socialista se distancia claramente y alcanza el 24,6% entre los mayores de 60 años.

Pisarello es la segunda opción para los votantes del PSC y Collboni lo es para los de ERC, pero los datos muestran que los electores no siempre eligen a su propio candidato cuando se les pregunta quién prefieren como alcalde. De hecho, los votantes de Junts se decantan por el candidato de Aliança Catalana antes que por el de su propio partido: Aragonès alcanza un 15,6% y Martí se queda en segunda posición con un 13,4%. Algo similar ocurre entre los electores del PP: un 17,1% elige a Collboni y un 16,4% a Sirera.

Collboni arrancará la precampaña electoral con la comodidad de ser un rostro reconocible para el electorado. Un 93,4% le identifica, un dato que le da ventaja sobre sus principales rivales. Alamany y Pisarello son conocidos por más del 60% de los barceloneses, pero suspenden con un 4,7 y un 4,4, respectivamente.

Sorprende especialmente el grado de conocimiento de Aragonès , similar al de sus competidores, pese a que se estrena como cabeza de cartel en una contienda electoral, aunque los barceloneses le suspenden (4,3). La apuesta del PP, Sirera , ronda el 63% de conocimiento, pero su apreciación cae al 3,1. Los menos conocidos por los encuestados son Martí y Oro-Pulido , con un 40% y un 31% respectivamente, aunque el primero obtiene un 4,0 y el segundo un 2,5. Todos los dirigentes registran un descenso en la percepción sobre su valoración, salvo Collboni, que se mantiene.
sources.headline: Sondeo GESOP: Collboni es el preferido como alcalde de Barcelona y el único candidato que aprueba

stories.headline: Catalonia plans a unified public-transport brand covering FGC and Rodalies services

sources.body:
La Generalitat unificarà en una sola marca el transport públic de Catalunya , que ara està fragmentat entre diferents identitats per un mateix servei, com per exemple les línies ferroviàries de Rodalies i Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat (FGC) o Exprés.cat, Connect o Clic.cat, en el cas del servei per carretera d'autobusos.

La licitació perquè una empresa s'ocupi de la definició i del disseny de la nova marca ja s'ha publicat. El contracte , segons recull el plec de clàusules administratives, té un pressupost base de licitació de 250.470 euros (IVA inclòs).

La previsió és que la nova marca es desplegui, també segons es recull a la licitació, en quatre grans àmbits conceptuals declinats de la marca principal: transport per carretera (autobús), mobilitat personal (bicicleta), transport ferroviari (tren) i infraestructures (tram, metro i logística).

Tot plegat amb l'objectiu de disposar d'una marca "coherent i unificada" que sigui més fàcil d'identificar per la ciutadania. El canvi, a més, es fa coincidint amb un moment en què s'està transformant el sistema de mobilitat de Catalunya , marcat per fites com el traspàs de Rodalies , el desplegament de la T-mobilitat o la modificació del servei d'autobusos interurbans.

El canvi es farà en tres etapes : en la primera, la marca unificada conviurà amb les marques actuals gràficament i visualment; en la segona, el pes visual passarà a ser de la marca mare, mantenint les denominacions actuals dels serveis, i serà en la tercera fase quan la unificació es farà efectiva.

El plec especifica que aquesta unificació afecta la identitat dels serveis, però en cap cas suposa una modificació pels operadors , que seguiran prestant el servei .

L' encàrrec no només inclou el disseny gràfic i el nom comercial, sinó també la creació d'un manual d'identitat corporativa, el nou sistema de senyalització física i la identitat auditiva del servei.

Només cinc agències especialitzades prèviament seleccionades passaran a la fase final. A més, el govern ha anunciat que, per fomentar la qualitat de les propostes , atorgarà una compensació econòmica de 6.000 euros a cadascuna de les empreses finalistes que no resultin adjudicatàries.

L'empresa a la qual s'acabi adjudicant l'encàrrec disposarà d'un termini d'execució de sis mesos per dissenyar aquesta nova arquitectura visual un cop formalitzat el contracte.
sources.headline: La Generalitat vol unificar en una sola marca el transport públic, inclosos FGC i Rodalies
